name: Frank Sherlock v0.8.2
body:
# v0.8.2

### Bug fixes

- **Face detection works again** (#12, thanks @ThiagooTavares for the detailed report): v0.8.1 shipped with mismatched ONNX components — the Rust bindings were silently upgraded by a dependency refresh to a version requiring ONNX Runtime 1.27+, while the app bundles 1.23. Face detection failed at initialization on every platform before processing a single image. The bindings are now pinned to the version matching the bundled runtime, and a new regression test performs the runtime-version handshake in CI on Linux, macOS, and Windows so this mismatch can never ship again.

- **Face detection failures are no longer silent**: any error in the face detection worker (model download failure, runtime initialization failure, model load failure) now appears as an error message in the UI instead of only being written to the log file, and a failed run no longer blocks retrying.

### Maintenance

- Updated rustls, clearing security advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0285.

### Test suite

- 345 Rust tests, 336 frontend tests.

## Install

| Platform | File |
|----------|------|
| Linux (AppImage) | `frank-sherlock_*_amd64.AppImage` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `frank-sherlock_*_aarch64.dmg` |
| Windows | `frank-sherlock_*_x64-setup.exe` |

### Prerequisites
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com) must be installed and running locally
- The app will prompt you to download the required model (`qwen2.5vl:7b`) on first launch

### Windows first launch
The installer is not code-signed. Windows SmartScreen may show a warning — click **More info** then **Run anyway** to proceed. You only need to do this once.

name: Frank Sherlock v0.8.1
body:
# v0.8.1

### Improvements

- **Ollama model override settings**: The vision model is no longer hardcoded — a settings override lets you pick which installed Ollama model handles classification, documented in the README.

- **Better default model on Windows NVIDIA 8GB GPUs**: Model selection now avoids recommending `qwen2.5vl:7b` on Windows machines with 8GB NVIDIA cards, where it does not fit comfortably in VRAM.

### Bug fixes

- **Scan no longer aborts on unreadable files** (#11, thanks @EduardoLacusta): A single file that could not be opened — restrictive ACLs, an exclusive lock held by another process, a cloud placeholder that fails to hydrate — killed the entire scan job with an unhelpful `io error: Access denied` and zero files indexed. Unreadable files are now skipped with a warning naming the path, the scan cursor advances past them so resume works, and a total is logged at the end of the phase. A follow-up fix ensures an already-indexed file that becomes temporarily unreadable keeps its index entry instead of being treated as deleted.

### Test suite

- Added App-level Vitest coverage for shell rendering, sidebar collapse, CLI auto-scan startup behavior, and tool-mode switching (#10, thanks @jadsongmatos).
- Hardened App test isolation with typed fixtures and restored spies between tests.
- New Rust regression tests for scans over unreadable files.
- 343 Rust tests, 332 frontend tests.

### Maintenance

- Updated Rust and frontend dependencies, clearing all outstanding `cargo audit` advisories (crossbeam-epoch, quick-xml, rkyv). Tauri moves to 2.11.x across the Rust and JS sides.
- Cleared Rust clippy warnings in PDF page detection, query parsing, video metadata extraction, Tauri command wrappers, and face-clustering tests so the CI clippy gate is green again.
- Fixed CI runtime compatibility in the GitHub Actions workflows.

name: Frank Sherlock v0.8.0
body:
# v0.8.0

### Bug fixes

- **Fix Windows startup crash** (#1): GUI apps spawning subprocesses (nvidia-smi, python, ffmpeg) caused visible console windows to flash in a loop on Windows. All 14 subprocess call sites now use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Added a 5-second timeout for nvidia-smi to prevent hangs on broken/updating drivers. GPU and Python detection are now deferred to first use (lazy `OnceLock`), so the window appears instantly. Replaced a `.expect()` panic on database init failure with a graceful error exit.

- **Fix model detection with `:latest` tag** (#2): When users install the model via `ollama pull qwen2.5vl` (without an explicit tag), Ollama stores it as `qwen2.5vl:latest`. The setup screen was doing an exact string match against `qwen2.5vl:7b`, asking the user to re-download an already-installed model.

- **Fix blank screen when adjusting near-duplicates threshold** (#3): Dragging the near-duplicates percentage slider caused the screen to go blank. The duplicates data was being cleared to `null` before the new API call completed, which unmounted the entire DuplicatesView component. Previous results now stay visible while re-fetching.

- **Fix ffmpeg not detected on macOS** (#4): macOS GUI apps launched from Finder or the Dock don't inherit the user's shell `$PATH`, so Homebrew-installed ffmpeg/ffprobe at `/opt/homebrew/bin` were invisible. Added well-known fallback path probing, matching the existing approach for Python detection.

- **Fix classification failing with different model variant** (#5): When the app recommends `qwen2.5vl:7b` but the user has a different variant installed (e.g. `:3b` or `:latest`), classification would silently fail because Ollama was asked for a model tag that didn't exist. The scan now resolves the actual installed model tag, and the setup screen accepts any variant from the same model family.

### Test suite

- 334 Rust tests (+12 new), 300 frontend tests (+1 new).

## Install

|----------|------|
| Linux (AppImage) | `frank-sherlock_*_amd64.AppImage` |

name: Frank Sherlock v0.7.0
body:
# v0.7.0

### Face detection and recognition
- Detect faces in your photo library using native ONNX models (SCRFD for detection, ArcFace for recognition) -- no Python or external services needed.
- Models are downloaded automatically on first use from the InsightFace buffalo_l pack.
- 512-dimensional face embeddings enable identity-aware clustering with cosine similarity (threshold 0.45).
- Faces are automatically clustered into people after detection. New faces are assigned to existing clusters or start new ones.
- FacesView shows all detected people as a card grid with representative face crops, editable names, and face count badges.
- Name people, merge duplicate identities, and remove false detections from the FacesView UI.
- Face crops are saved as 150px JPEGs in the cache directory.
- Search by person: `face:alice`, `face:"Full Name"`, or `face:42` (by person ID).
- Face detection is triggered per-folder from the right-click context menu.
- Status bar shows face detection progress with download/loading/detecting phases.
- Re-cluster confirmation guard prevents accidental overwrites of manual name assignments.

### Preview keyboard navigation
- Press Space to close the preview modal (previously Space only opened it).
- ArrowLeft/ArrowRight navigate to previous/next image while preview is open (single-item mode).
- Arrow keys are ignored in multi-image collage/comparison mode.
- Keyboard events skip handling when a video element or input field has focus.

### Setup modal install links
- When Ollama is not detected, the setup modal now shows a clickable "install" link that opens the Ollama download page in the system browser.
- When Python is not available for OCR, a clickable "install Python" link opens the Python downloads page.
- Uses the official `tauri-plugin-opener` for cross-platform URL opening.

### Internal improvements
- App.tsx refactored to extract 5 feature hooks (`useAutoUpdate`, `useFaceDetection`, `useAlbumManager`, `useSmartFolderManager`, `useDuplicatesManager`), reducing orchestration complexity.
- Face feature code extracted into shared helpers and CSS modules.
- Thumbnail generation now respects EXIF orientation data.
- Database migrations 11-12 add face detection tables (`face_detections`, `people`) with proper indexes.
- Test suite expanded to 322 Rust tests and 299 frontend tests.

## Install

|----------|------|
| Linux (AppImage) | `frank-sherlock_*_amd64.AppImage` |

name: Frank Sherlock v0.6.0
body:
# v0.6.0

### Video support
- Scan and classify video files: MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, WebM, WMV, FLV, M4V, TS, MPG, MPEG.
- Videos are classified via keyframe extraction and LLM analysis — black frames are automatically skipped.
- Thumbnails are generated from representative keyframes. A play icon badge appears on video tiles.
- Embedded and external subtitles (.srt) are parsed and indexed for full-text search.
- Video metadata (duration, resolution, codecs) is shown in the Properties panel.
- Preview modal plays videos inline via a local streaming server with HTTP Range support.
- Search recognizes `video`, `movie`, `episode`, `film`, and `tv show` as media type keywords.
- Requires ffmpeg/ffprobe (optional) — the setup screen shows availability status.

### Three-phase scanning
- The scan pipeline is now discovering → thumbnailing → classifying → cleanup (was two phases).
- Files appear in the grid immediately with thumbnails while LLM classification runs in the background. Unclassified files show with confidence 0 and extension-inferred media types.
- Thumbnailing and classifying phases each support independent cancel and resume.
- Phase-specific progress: "Thumbnailing X/Y" with add/mod/moved stats, "Classifying X/Y" with ETA.

### Refresh Metadata (no Ollama required)
- Right-click a folder and choose "Refresh Metadata" to discover new/modified files and generate thumbnails without running LLM classification. Works even when Ollama is not running.
- "Rescan" remains the full pipeline including classification.

### Directory tree browser
- Clicking a root folder in the sidebar reveals a collapsible directory tree below it.
- Click any subdirectory to filter the grid to that path. Click again to deselect.
- Children are lazy-loaded one level at a time from the database.
- Clicking a subdirectory fills `subdir:path` visibly in the search input, so you can further refine the query or save it as a smart folder.

### Search improvements
- FTS5 porter stemmer: searching for "running" now matches "run", "runs", "runner", etc.
- LIKE substring fallback: when FTS returns no results, a case-insensitive substring search is attempted automatically.
- Media-type trigger words are stripped from the FTS query to avoid false positives.
- Fixed placeholder text advertising non-existent syntax.
- Help modal documents `album:`, `subdir:` prefixes and the stemming/fallback behavior.

## Install

name: Frank Sherlock v0.5.0
body:
# v0.5.0

Read [Release Notes](https://github.com/akitaonrails/FrankSherlock/blob/master/releases/v0.5.0.md).

Support for Arch/AUR package!

### In-app updates
- The app now checks for updates on startup and shows a button in the sidebar when a new version is available. Click to download and install without leaving the app.
- Manual "Check for Updates" button in the Tools section for on-demand checks.
- Uses Tauri's built-in updater with signed update artifacts — the app verifies the signature before applying anything.

### Scan progress fix
- The progress bar and file counter during phase 2 (classification) now update after every file instead of batching every 50. With LLM classification taking a few seconds per file, the old batching made progress look frozen for minutes.

### UI
- The Tools section (Find Duplicates, PDF Passwords, Check for Updates) is now pinned above the Info panel in the sidebar. Content lists (roots, albums, smart folders) scroll independently underneath.

### CI
- Release notes are now loaded from `releases/vX.Y.Z.md` and included in GitHub Releases automatically.
